respuesta.razonamiento: The architecture shows an automated, cost-optimized deployment pipeline and streaming environment for IHS Markit's 'Kingdom' petrotechnical software training. An instructor triggers AWS CloudFormation, which uses a custom resource to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Lambda uses AWS Systems Manager to execute a script on an EC2 instance. The EC2 instance connects to Amazon AppStream 2.0 Image Builder to customize the image (including adding a session script to mount Amazon FSx) and signals back to CloudFormation's wait condition. Once provisioned, students access Kingdom via a browser streaming URL through AppStream, which accesses project storage on Amazon FSx and database data on Amazon RDS.
respuesta.nombre: IHS Markit Virtual Software Training with AppStream 2.0 and CloudFormation

edges.notes: Students access Kingdom application via streaming URL

edges.notes: Session script mounts FSx project storage
edges.respaldo: Drawn line from AppStream to FSx labeled 'session script'; transcript: 'modify a session script in the image builder which will make sure that the FSx that just got provisioned in CloudFormation is mounted'.
Drawn line extending to RDS; transcript: 'and then rds for the database and basically all of that together makes Kingdom run'.
